In other words, when a lot of observations are available,\r\nthe prior information plays a smaller role.</p>\r\n</div>\r\n<h1 id=\"sec:Information theory\">Information theory</h1>\r\n<h2 We\r\nhave that</p>\r\n<p><math display=\"block\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>\u2113</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>\u03b8</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>\u2026</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>\u2212</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mover><mi>h</mi><mo accent=\"true\">\u203e</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>\u03b8</mi></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\ell (\\theta,x_1,\\dots,x_n) =-n H(\\bar h, p_{\\theta})</annotation></semantics></math></p>\r\n<p>So maximizing\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>\u2113</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>\u03b8</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>\u2026</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\ell (\\theta,x_1,\\dots,x_n)</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nis the same as minimizing the cross entropy between the empirical\r\nprobability and the model. Indeed, since\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mover><mi>h</mi><mo the\r\nmodel.</p>\r\n</div>\r\n<div id=\"th:The Gibbs inequality\" class=\"theorem\">\r\n<p><strong>Theorem 11</strong> (<strong>The Gibbs inequality</strong>).\r\n</p>\r\n<div style=\"color: Thus, we can extend the sum to\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation inequality), we know\r\nthat\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>\u2032</mo></msup><mo stretchy=\"false\" Upper Bound:\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>*</mo></msup><mo>\u2264</mo><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">L^* \\le H(P) + 1</annotation></semantics></math></strong></p>\r\n<div class=\"proof\">\r\n<p><em>Proof.</em> We construct a specific code (often called the\r\nShannon code) to show that a code satisfying the bound exists.</p>\r\n<p>For each symbol\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">s_i</annotation></semantics></math>,\r\nlet us choose the integer length:</p>\r\n<p><math display=\"block\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>\u2113</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"true\" form=\"prefix\">\u2308</mo><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">log</mi><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mfrac><mo stretchy=\"true\" form=\"postfix\">\u2309</mo></mrow><mi>.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\ell_i = \\left\\lceil \\log \\frac{1}{p_i} \\right\\rceil.</annotation></semantics></math></p>\r\n<p>First, we must check if a prefix code with these lengths exists. We\r\ncheck the Kraft inequality:</p>\r\n<p><math display=\"block\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><munderover><mo>\u2211</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>\u2212</mi><msub><mi>\u2113</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo>\u2211</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>\u2212</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">\u2308</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">log</mi><mo>&#8289;</mo></mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mfrac><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">\u2309</mo></mrow></msup><mo>\u2264</mo><munderover><mo>\u2211</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>\u2212</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">log</mi><mo>&#8289;</mo></mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo>\u2211</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\sum_{i=1}^n 2^{-\\ell_i} \r\n  = \\sum_{i=1}^n 2^{-\\lceil \\log \\frac{1}{p_i} \\rceil} \r\n  \\le \\sum_{i=1}^n 2^{-\\log \\frac{1}{p_i}} \r\n  = \\sum_{i=1}^n p_i \r\n  = 1.</annotation></semantics></math></p>\r\n<p>Since the sum is\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mo>\u2264</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\le 1</annotation></semantics></math>,\r\nby the converse of the Kraft\u2013McMillan theorem, a prefix code with these\r\nlengths exists.</p>\r\n<p>Now, we compute the expected length of this code. Using the property\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>\u2264</mo><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">\u2308</mo><mi>x</mi><mo 1</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>\r\n<p><math display=\"block\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign=\"right\" style=\"text-align: right;   &amp;= \\sum_{i=1}^n p_i \\left\\lceil \\log \\frac{1}{p_i} \\right\\rceil \\\\\r\n       &amp;&lt; \\sum_{i=1}^n p_i \\left( \\log \\frac{1}{p_i} + 1 \\right) \\\\\r\n       &amp;= \\underbrace{\\sum_{i=1}^n p_i \\log \\frac{1}{p_i}}_{H(P)} + \\underbrace{\\sum_{i=1}^n p_i}_{1}.\r\n\\end{align*}</annotation></semantics></math></p>\r\n<p>Thus,</p>\r\n<p><math display=\"block\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>H</mi><mo xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>*</mo></msup><mo>\u2264</mo><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" id=\"disc:Entropy and DKL as code length\" class=\"discussion\">\r\n<p><strong>Discussion 5</strong> (<strong>Entropy and DKL as code\r\nlength</strong>). </p>\r\n<ul>\r\n<li><p><math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">H(P)</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nis (approximately) the average length of an optimal code for symbols of\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">S</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nunder the distribution\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">P</annotation></semantics></math>.</p></li>\r\n<li><p>Breakdown of terms:</p>\r\n<ul>\r\n<li><p><math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mfrac><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\frac{1}{p_i}</annotation></semantics></math>:\r\nquantity (inverse probability / information content).</p></li>\r\n<li><p><math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">log</mi><mo>&#8289;</mo></mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\log \\frac{1}{p_i}</annotation></semantics></math>:\r\ntree depth (codeword length) in an optimal code.</p></li>\r\n</ul></li>\r\n<li><p>If a code is optimized for a distribution\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">Q</annotation></semantics></math>,\r\nbut the source actually follows distribution\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">P</annotation></semantics></math>:\r\n<math display=\"block\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>\ud835\udd3c</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">[</mo><mi>\u2113</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">]</mo><mo>=</mo><munder><mo>\u2211</mo><mi>i</mi></munder><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">log</mi><mo>&#8289;</mo></mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mi>.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbb{E}[\\ell(c)] = \\sum_i p_i \\log \\frac{1}{q_i} = H(P,Q).</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nConsequently, the Kullback\u2013Leibler divergence:\r\n<math display=\"block\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">K</mi><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">L</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mo>\u2212</mo><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo></mrow><annotation if the code is optimized for\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">Q</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nrather than the true distribution\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">P</annotation></semantics></math>.</p></li>\r\n<li><p><strong>Remember that:</strong> \u201cThe differential entropy cannot\r\nbe approximated by the entropy of a discrete approximation of the\r\ndensity.\u201d</p>\r\n<p>A consequence is that the <strong>differential entropy does not have\r\nan interpretation in terms of code length</strong>.</p></li>\r\n</ul>\r\n</div>\r\n<div id=\"disc:Entropy and information\" class=\"discussion\">\r\n<p><strong>Discussion 6</strong> (<strong>Entropy and\r\ninformation</strong>). </p>\r\n<ul>\r\n<li><p>Consider a uniform distribution on a set of\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>N</mi></msup><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">2^N</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nelements. In an optimal code, every element is coded by a string\r\n(sequence) of length\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">log</mi><mo>&#8289;</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>N</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">N = \\log_2 2^N</annotation></semantics></math>.</p></li>\r\n<li><p>When trying to describe an element,\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">N</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nbits of information are needed.</p></li>\r\n<li><p>If we are given the first\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">n</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nbits describing an element, only\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>\u2212</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">N-n</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nbits are then needed to identify the element.</p></li>\r\n<li><p>Hence, the <strong>information gain</strong> is\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">n</annotation></semantics></math>.</p></li>\r\n<li><p>Here, the probability of the event described (fixing the first\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">n</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nbits) is:\r\n<math display=\"block\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>\u2212</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>N</mi></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>\u2212</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup><mi>.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">p = \\frac{2^{N-n}}{2^N} = 2^{-n}.</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nWe say that the information associated with the event is\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">log</mi><mo>&#8289;</mo></mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>p</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">n=\\log \\frac{1}{p}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p></li>\r\n<li><p>In general, we define the <strong>information content</strong> of\r\nan event\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>E</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">E</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nas\r\n<math display=\"block\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">log</mi><mo>&#8289;</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy=\"true\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy=\"true\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>\u2212</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">log</mi><mo>&#8289;</mo></mrow><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mi>.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">I(E) = \\log\\left(\\frac{1}{P(E)}\\right) = -\\log P(E).</annotation></semantics></math></p></li>\r\n</ul>\r\n</div>\r\n<div id=\"def:Huffman codes\" class=\"definition\">\r\n<p><strong>Definition 37</strong> (<strong>Huffman codes</strong>). </p>\r\n<div style=\"color: blue\">\r\n<hr />\r\n<p><strong>Construction</strong></p>\r\n</div>\r\n<p><br />\r\n</p>\r\n<ul>\r\n<li><p><math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">S</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nis a finite set (source alphabet) with a probability distribution\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">P</annotation></semantics></math>.</p></li>\r\n<li><p>A <strong>Huffman code</strong>\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">c</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nis constructed recursively (Bottom-Up construction):</p>\r\n<ol>\r\n<li><p><strong>Base Case:</strong> If\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">|</mo><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">|S|=2</annotation></semantics></math>,\r\nassign\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">0</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nto one symbol and\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">1</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nto the other.</p></li>\r\n<li><p><strong>Recursive Step:</strong></p>\r\n<ul>\r\n<li><p>Identify the two symbols\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">s_i, s_j</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nwith the lowest probabilities\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">p_i, p_j</annotation></semantics></math>.</p></li>\r\n<li><p>Merge them into a new \u201cmeta-symbol\u201d\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">s_{ij}</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nwith probability\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">p_{ij} = p_i + p_j</annotation></semantics></math>.</p></li>\r\n<li><p>Define a reduced source\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mo>\u2032</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>\\</mo><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">{</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">}</mo><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mo>\u222a</mo><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">{</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">S&#39; = (S \\setminus \\{s_i, s_j\\}) \\cup \\{s_{ij}\\}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p></li>\r\n<li><p>Construct a Huffman code\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><msup><mi>c</mi><mo>\u2032</mo></msup><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">c&#39;</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nfor\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mo>\u2032</mo></msup><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">S&#39;</annotation></semantics></math>.</p></li>\r\n</ul></li>\r\n<li><p><strong>Code Construction (Back-propagation):</strong> Once the\r\ncode\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><msup><mi>c</mi><mo>\u2032</mo></msup><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">c&#39;</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nfor the reduced set is known, the codes for the original symbols are:\r\n<math display=\"block\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>c</mi><mo>\u2032</mo></msup><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mo>\u22c5</mo><mn>0</mn><mspace width=\"1.0em\"></mspace><mtext mathvariant=\"normal\">(append 0 to the parent\u2019s code)</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">c(s_i) = c&#39;(s_{ij}) \\cdot 0 \\quad \\text{(append 0 to the parent&#39;s code)}</annotation></semantics></math>\r\n<math display=\"block\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>c</mi><mo>\u2032</mo></msup><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mo>\u22c5</mo><mn>1</mn><mspace width=\"1.0em\"></mspace><mtext mathvariant=\"normal\">(append 1 to the parent\u2019s code)</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">c(s_j) = c&#39;(s_{ij}) \\cdot 1 \\quad \\text{(append 1 to the parent&#39;s code)}</annotation></semantics></math>\r\n<em>(where\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>\u22c5</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\cdot</annotation></semantics></math>\r\ndenotes concatenation).</em></p></li>\r\n</ol></li>\r\n</ul>\r\n<p><strong>Theorem (Optimality):</strong></p>\r\n<p>If\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mtext mathvariant=\"normal\">Huff</mtext></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">L_{\\text{Huff}}</annotation></semantics></math>\r\ndenotes the expected length of a Huffman code and\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">L(C)</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nis the expected length of any other prefix code for the same\r\ndistribution, then:</p>\r\n<p><math display=\"block\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mtext mathvariant=\"normal\">Huff</mtext></msub><mo>\u2264</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mi>.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">L_{\\text{Huff}} \\le L(C).</annotation></semantics></math></p>\r\n<p>We will not prove this result. Because Huffman codes are optimal,\r\nthey satisfy the tight bounds of Shannon\u2019s Source Coding Theorem:\r\n<math display=\"block\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mo>\u2264</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mtext mathvariant=\"normal\">Huff</mtext></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">H(P) \\le L_{\\text{Huff}} &lt; H(P) + 1.</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nThis confirms that Huffman coding is an <em>entropic code</em>: it\r\ncompresses data to within 1 bit of the theoretical limit per symbol.</p>\r\n<div style=\"color: blue\">\r\n<hr />\r\n<p><strong>Example</strong></p>\r\n</div>\r\n<p><br />\r\n<strong>Source Probabilities and Reduction Steps:</strong></p>\r\n<div \\log P(h) &amp; = H(\\bar{h}) - H(\\bar{h}, P) + o(1)\\\\\r\n      &amp;= -D_{\\mathrm{KL}}(\\bar{h} \\,\\|\\, P) + Uniformity can be\r\ninterpreted as a measure of disorder.\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>\u03b4</mi></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">P = \\delta</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nrepresents the highest level of order. When\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">P</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nis uniform, every element occupies the same proportion, which is\r\ninterpreted as \u201cmaximal disorder\u201d. Many phenomena have a tendency to\r\nincrease uniformity\r\n(<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mo>\u223c</mo><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\sim</annotation></semantics></math>\r\ndisorder) as time evolves. It is particularly true in physics. Consider\r\na phenomenon to which we associate a probability\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">P_0</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nat time\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">0</annotation></semantics></math>.\r\nAs time evolves, the probability evolves to\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>\u2026</mi></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">P_1,P_2,\\dots</annotation></semantics></math>.\r\nIf the phenomenon increases uniformity, the distribution\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">P_t</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nmight stabilize close to a point of maximal uniformity. If the\r\nphenomenon preserves some constraints\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">C</annotation></semantics></math>,\r\nthe uniformity is maximized under these constraints. We have then good\r\nreason to expect that (when it exists)</p>\r\n<p><math display=\"block\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>\u221e</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">argmax</mi><mo>&#8289;</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>\u2208</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></msub><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mi>.</mi></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">P_{\\infty} = \\operatorname{argmax}_{P \\in C} H(P).</annotation></semantics></math></p>\r\n</div>\r\n<div id=\"disc:Simple random walk\" class=\"discussion\">\r\n<p><strong>Discussion 10</strong> (<strong>Simple random walk</strong>).\r\n</p>\r\n<div style=\"color: blue\">\r\n<hr xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>\u2124</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nwith probability\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">0.5</annotation></semantics></math>.\r\nLet\r\n<math random variable taking values in\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>\u2124</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math>,\r\nmodeling the position of the person at time\r\n<math display=\"inline\" style=\"color: blue\">\r\n<hr />\r\n<p><strong>law of\r\n<math display=\"inline\" = 0\r\n\\qquad\\text{and}\\qquad\r\n\\sum_k v_k^2\\, h(k) = v^2 .</annotation></semantics></math></p>\r\n</div>\r\n<div id=\"rem:2 levels of probabilities\" class=\"remark\">\r\n<p><strong>Remark deterministic\r\nprocess</strong></p>\r\n</div>\r\n<p><br />\r\nThe last exemple has similarities in nature with exemple 2. The\r\nmicrostate will now refer to the positions and speeds of the collection\r\nof balls. This time the micorstate\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">x_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nat time\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">t+1</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nis completely determined by the macrostate at time\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">t</annotation></semantics></math>.\r\nNote that even in that case, the uncertainty about the initialization\r\nligitimates the modeling of microstates with random variables\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">X_t</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>\r\n<p>A histogram\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">h_t</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nis computed at each step, and we consider its evolution along a\r\ntrajectory. We observed that the phenomenon repeats itself on all the\r\ntried realisation (= initial conditions).</p>\r\n<div style=\"color: blue\">\r\n<hr />\r\n<p><strong>Moral</strong></p>\r\n</div>\r\n<p><br />\r\nEventhough the 3 examples fall under the umbrella of the maximum entropy\r\nprinciple, it is important to note that they are of a relatively\r\ndifferent nature. This partly explains why we proved that the entropy\r\nincreases in the first example but we only considered simulation for\r\nexample 2 and 3.</p>\r\n</div>\r\n<h1 id=\"sec:Exponential \\psi</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nits Hessian.</p>\r\n<div style=\"color: blue\">\r\n<hr />\r\n<p><strong>Example: exponential distributions</strong></p>\r\n</div>\r\n<p><br />\r\nConsider the ]-\\infty,0[.</annotation></semantics></math></p>\r\n<p>Hence</p>\r\n<p><math display=\"block\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>\u03c8</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>\u03c8</mi><mo>\u2033</mo></msup><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>\u03b8</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>\u03bb</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>\u03b8</mi></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" p(x)\\,\\log\\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}</annotation></semantics></math></p>\r\n<p>in the discrete case, or with integrals in the continuous case. For a\r\ngeneral pair\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">(P,Q)</annotation></semantics></math>,\r\nthere is no obvious simplification of this formula. However, for two\r\nmembers of the <em>same</em> exponential family, the expression becomes\r\nmuch simpler.</p>\r\n<p>Consider a one-dimensional exponential family with carrier\r\n<math Kullback-Leibler divergence between two members\r\nof the same exponential family can be written purely in terms of the\r\nnatural parameter, the expectation parameter and the log-partition\r\nfunction.</p>\r\n<p><strong>Remark (to go further):</strong> The fact that the\r\nKullback-Leibler divergence simplifies on exponential families is an\r\ninstance of a more general phenomenon: how the Bregman divergence\r\nassociated with a convex function\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">F</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nbehaves when restricted to the set of minimizers of\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">F</annotation></semantics></math>\r\nunder linear constraints.</p>\r\n</div>\r\n<h2 id=\"subsec:Estimation in an exponential family\">Estimation in an\r\nexponential family</h2>\r\n<div id=\"th:Fisher information in an exponential family\"\r\nclass=\"theorem\">\r\n<p><strong>Theorem 19</strong> (Fisher information in an exponential\r\nfamily). </p>\r\n<div style=\"color: blue\">\r\n<hr />\r\n<p><strong>Natural parameter</strong></p>\r\n</div>\r\n<p><br />\r\nConsider a one-parameter exponential family</p>\r\n<p><math display=\"block\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>\u03b8</mi></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>\u03b8</mi><mo form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mspace width=\"0.167em\"></mspace><mrow><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">exp</mi><mo>&#8289;</mo></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>\u03b8</mi><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mspace Z(\\theta).</annotation></semantics></math></p>\r\n<p>Then</p>\r\n<p><math display=\"block\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi \\log h(x) - \\psi(\\theta),</annotation></semantics></math></p>\r\n<p>so the score is</p>\r\n<p><math display=\"block\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo form=\"postfix\">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>\u2202</mi><mrow><mi>\u2202</mi><mi>\u03b8</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mi \\psi&#39;(\\theta).</annotation></semantics></math></p>\r\n<p>If\r\n<math display=\"inline\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>\u223c</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>\u03b8</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">X\\sim xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML\"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\" form=\"prefix\">(</mo><mi>\u03b8</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\"
